title.value: Asymptotically Optimal Early Termination for Dishonest Majority Broadcast
Asymptotically Optimal Early Termination for Dishonest Majority Broadcast

abstract.value: Deterministic broadcast protocols among n parties tolerating t corruptions require min{f + 2, t + 1} rounds, where f ≤ t is the actual number of corruptions in an execution of the protocol. We provide the first protocol which is optimally resilient, adaptively secure, and asymptotically matches this lower bound for any t < (1-ε)n. By contrast, the best known algorithm in this regime by Loss and Nielsen (EURO-CRYPT'24) always requires O(min{f 2 , t}) rounds. Our main technical tool is a generalization of the notion of polarizer introduced by Loss and Nielsen, which allows parties to obtain transferable cryptographic evidence of missing messages with fewer rounds of interaction.
